article.title: When Disk Diet caches return: review before cleaning again
article.primaryIntent: Understand a returning cache after a category clean, distinguish rebuildable data from personal Downloads, and decide whether to investigate recurring growth.
outline: Lead: returning caches alone do not establish failed cleanup; attribute explanation to vendor FAQ C9
Top visual: official Basic Clean app figure only after rights clearance
Separate caches, Downloads and unused applications; category membership is not deletion permission
Check access and distribution before interpreting low scan totals; do not publish legacy System Preferences instructions as Tahoe steps
Use Xcode-specific documented scope rather than promising package-manager coverage
Later visual: labelled Breathing Room Space example; explain source-level investigation versus measured evidence
Decision aid: rebuildable known cache / personal files / unknown or recurring growth; stop and inspect when ownership is unclear
article.length: Earned, approximately 900-1400 words; no invented statistics, FAQs or execution narrative
article.description: Disk Diet's FAQ says some caches can return immediately. Review the category and data you need before repeating cleanup or investigating recurring growth.
article.toolLinkPolicy: Only link a related cache checklist or tool after its actual route and behavior are verified; do not invent a route.

structure: Bounded conclusion with 'Breathing Room, which we build' disclosure

diskDiet: Documented ten-area category workflow and unused-app list; one-time direct offer, not subscription (C4,C6,C7).
Advertised Intel/Apple silicon and macOS 11.5 direct support; vendor notarization claim (C2,C3,C10).
Different App Store permission/helper setup; no verified equivalent of process grouping, recurring-growth monitoring or broad package-manager adapters. Unknown is not absent (C8).
breathingRoom: Source-level storage ownership views, grouped activity and developer-cache investigation may suit diagnosis of recurring growth (B2), not proof of better cleanup.
Free local preview plus optional hosted AI Care; disclose Python, authentication/network, data sharing, non-notarized preview and runtime-validation limits (B1,B2).
Daily care needs running app and exact approvals; optional automatic Ruff exception must not be erased by blanket per-action approval wording.
